scope: Dev cohorts only (ham_dev, pad_adapt). Frozen features, balanced-LR protocol, same folds. No holdout or target_test opened. CPU only, <=4 concurrent, 3 BLAS threads.
self_checks: Refit at the recorded C/tau reproduces every job JSON pooled OOF macro-F1 (max abs diff 0.0, all 9 arms, all 12 jobs). R4 tau=0 reproduces the balanced baseline exactly (asserted in-script).

variant_count.note: 16 reader configurations (9 arms + 6 R4 tau points + 1 R4 joint) evaluated on dev for each of 2 feature sets, 2 cohorts, 3 encoder seeds. All were reported; I did not pick a winner on holdout. Earlier per-class offset arms (negative) are outside this count.

gap_definition: train_minus_oof = mean over outer folds of macro-F1 on the fold train rows minus pooled OOF macro-F1. inner_minus_oof = mean inner-CV selection score (macro-F1 for macro_f1 arms; bACC/minrec for the others, so only macro_f1 arms are comparable) minus pooled OOF macro-F1. Inner folds train on 2/3 of the outer train, so inner scores are pessimistic by construction.
r4_decision_rule: R4 is a candidate only if, for every encoder seed, the seed-mean macro-F1 delta of r4_joint vs the balanced-LR baseline is >= +0.005 AND the target minority recall (HAM mel, PAD SCC) rises >= 0.01 while its error endpoint (HAM mel->NV, PAD SCC->BCC) does not worsen by more than 0.02. Otherwise R4 is negative. Stated before the run.
r4_result: NEGATIVE in all four tag-cohort blocks. Joint (tau,C) gives macro-F1 deltas of -0.006 to +0.007 across encoder seeds; no block meets the rule.
r4_curves_note: Monotone trade-off in tau: tau up lowers mel->NV (HAM 448 0.19 -> 0.07 at tau 1) and raises mel recall (+0.02), while macro-F1 falls (tau 0 ~0.61 -> tau 1 ~0.50, mean of 3 encoder seeds). PAD: tau up raises SCC recall and lowers SCC->BCC, macro-F1 falls. Same frontier as the sample-weight arms.
